# Independent audit: planar three-cap overlap stability


overlap and equality theorems explicitly cited by the source.

Audited source:
planar-three-cap-overlap-uniform-stability-simplex-chains.md.
This is a local ordinary planar stability theorem and a conditional
budget localization inequality. It does not close an OC argument.

## 1. Normalization and compactness

The maximum inscribed triangle exists by compactness of K cubed.
Mapping its vertices to the standard triangle preserves all relative
areas and cap-cover relations. Replacing its ith vertex by a point x
gives area |lambda_i(x)|/2, so maximality yields all three
|lambda_i|<=1 constraints.

Their intersection is exactly the triangle with vertices
(1,1),(1,-1),(-1,1): in Cartesian coordinates they are
-1<=x,y<=1 and 0<=x+y<=2. Thus it lies strictly inside the
radius-two ball. The normalized bodies contain the fixed
standard triangle and have area at least 1/2.

The support functions are uniformly bounded and uniformly Lipschitz.
Their uniform subsequential limit is the support function of a
compact convex body between the same two fixed triangles. For
example, any support maximum in the sequence has a convergent
subsequence of maximizing points, which verifies attainment of
the limiting support value. Every inscribed limit triangle is
approximated vertexwise, preserving the maximum-area bound.
This verifies the claimed compact normalized class without
requiring a continuous choice of maximizing triangles.

Clipping b below -2 changes only a full-cap trace, since every
body lies in the radius-two ball. The compact unit-normal/
bounded-offset parameter space is therefore valid even for
full traces. Positive cap mass excludes an empty positive-area
trace at offset two.

## 2. Limits, equality, and the positive modulus

Indicators of normalized bodies converge away from the limiting
boundary, and halfplane indicators converge away from the
limiting line. Both exceptional sets have area zero. The common
bounded containing ball justifies dominated convergence for all
three captured areas and the body area. Area denominators stay
at least 1/2. Closed covers pass to the limit by approximating
each point and extracting one of three fixed indices.

The lower bound A_i>=tau V therefore gives a compact class
without disappearing caps. On this class, the cited positive-cap
equality theorem identifies a triangle with its canonical centroid
vertex caps. The maximum-inscribed-triangle normalization then
forces that triangle to equal T: it contains T and itself has
area at most 1/2. The listed canonical parameters are correct:
x>=1/3, y>=1/3, x+y<=2/3.

All three terms of D are continuous, including the minimum over
the six cap permutations. The closed bad set D>=eta is compact.
If nonempty, its attained minimum of E/V cannot be zero, by the
equality classification. Taking half this positive minimum gives
the claimed strict conclusion under E/V<=epsilon. The empty
bad-set convention is harmless, including tau>1.

The conclusion is uniform over every choice of a maximum-area
inscribed triangle, because every such choice lies in the same
normalized class. These independent affine normalizations are
used only for the single-body theorem and do not alter a mixed
lattice family.

## 3. Tightening surplus

For componentwise A=A'+delta with delta_i>=0,

    min A-min A'<=max delta_i<=sum delta_i.

Hence

    [sum A-(3/4)min A]-[sum A'-(3/4)min A']
       >=(1/4)sum delta_i.

The tightened concurrent cover still covers, so its bracket is
at least V by the underlying overlap theorem. This proves
E>=sum delta_i/4. Consequently each tightened area is at least
tau V-4E, giving tau V/2 when E<=tau V/8.

## 4. Subthreshold localization and constants

The ordinary cover bound on every owned fiber gives
M<=3kB, so the premise
kB<=(4/9-delta)M implies delta<=1/9.
For eta in (0,delta), the coefficient 1/9-eta is positive.

On each good fiber, stability gives average captured area at
least (4/9-eta)V_z; on every remaining fiber the cover bound
gives V_z/3. The total remaining mass is at most
W_tau+E_tot/epsilon, because failures of the minimum-cap
condition enter W_tau and failures of the surplus condition
satisfy V_z<E_z/epsilon.

The sum of owned cap areas is at most the sum of the 3k global
cap occurrences, at most 3kB. Repeated caps cause no problem:
each occurrence has its own bound and only its assigned
fibers are charged. Thus

    kB >= (4/9-eta)M
              -(1/9-eta)(W_tau+E_tot/epsilon).

Combining with the stated upper budget gives exactly

    W_tau+E_tot/epsilon
        >=[(delta-eta)/(1/9-eta)]M.

Both signs and constants agree. No claim in the source eliminates
either term, and no hidden assumption turns this local alternative
into the full mixed-integer inequality. No correction is required.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
